record.paper_title: List homomorphism problems for signed trees
record.original_question: For a fixed signed graph H with possible loops, where signed-graph homomorphisms are considered up to switching of the input signature, consider List-S-Hom(H): given an input signed graph G and a list L(v) of allowed target vertices for each vertex v of G, decide whether there is a signed-graph homomorphism from G to H sending every v to an element of L(v). Which fixed signed graphs H make List-S-Hom(H) polynomial-time solvable, and which make it NP-complete? Can the polynomial side be described by a natural graph-theoretic structure analogous to bi-arc graphs for unsigned graph list homomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Definition 3. Let Hb be a fixed signed graph. The list homomorphism problem List-S-Hom(Hb) takes as input a signed graph Gb with lists L(v) ⊆ V (H) for every v ∈ V (G), and asks whether there exists a homomorphism f of Gb to Hb such that f(v) ∈ L(v) for every v ∈ V (G).

We conclude that our problems List-S-Hom(Hb) fit into the general constraint satisfaction framework, and therefore it follows from [9, 31] that dichotomy holds for problems List-S-Hom(Hb). We therefore ask which problems List-S-Hom(Hb) are polynomial-time solvable and which are NP-complete.

The structure of the signed trees in the polynomial cases is interesting, suggesting that the class of general signed graphs for which the problems are polynomial may have nice structure, analogous to the so-called bi-arc graphs (which characterized the polynomial cases of list homomorphisms to unsigned graphs).

It seems difficult to give a full combinatorial classification of the complexity of list homomorphism problems for general signed graphs. We have accomplished this for signed trees (with possible loops).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $\hat H = (H, \sigma)$ where $H = (V(H), E(H))$ is a graph (loops allowed) and $\sigma : E(H) \to \{+, -\}$ assigns a sign to each edge. A switch at a vertex $v$ replaces $\sigma(e)$ by $-\sigma(e)$ on every edge $e$ incident with $v$ (loops at $v$ are unchanged). Two signed graphs on the same underlying graph are switch-equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of vertex switchings. A homomorphism of signed graphs $f : \hat G \to \hat H$ is a map $f : V(G) \to V(H)$ that, after some switching of $\hat G$, sends edges to edges and preserves signs.

For a fixed signed graph $\hat H$ (loops permitted) define the problem $\mathrm{List\text{-}S\text{-}Hom}(\hat H)$:
- Input: a signed graph $\hat G$ together with lists $L(v) \subseteq V(H)$ for every $v \in V(G)$.
- Question: does there exist a signed-graph homomorphism $f : \hat G \to \hat H$ such that $f(v) \in L(v)$ for every $v \in V(G)$?

It is known that $\mathrm{List\text{-}S\text{-}Hom}(\hat H)$ admits a P/NP-complete dichotomy as $\hat H$ varies. The problem is to give an explicit combinatorial classification of the signed graphs $\hat H$ for which $\mathrm{List\text{-}S\text{-}Hom}(\hat H)$ is solvable in polynomial time (and for which it is NP-complete), and in particular to determine whether the polynomial-time cases are characterized by a natural graph-theoretic structure analogous to the bi-arc graph characterization that describes the polynomial cases of list homomorphism to unsigned graphs.
artifact.category_tag: List homomorphism dichotomy for signed graphs
artifact.status_search_result: A general dichotomy follows from CSP results, but an explicit combinatorial classification for arbitrary signed graphs is not yet established. Partial classifications have been obtained: for signed trees (Bok, Brewster, Feder, Hell, Jedličková), for reflexive signed graphs, for irreflexive signed graphs, for semi-balanced signed graphs (Kim–Siggers conjecture, since verified in several cases), and for separable signed graphs. A bi-arc-style structural characterization for general signed graphs remains an active area of research without a full combinatorial answer as of 2024–2025.

status_evidence.title: Min Orderings and List Homomorphism Dichotomies for Graphs and Signed Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Classifications of list homomorphism complexity for signed graphs in special classes; conjecture of Kim and Siggers verified for reflexive and irreflexive signed graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Partial dichotomy classifications established for several classes of signed graphs.

status_evidence.title: List Homomorphisms to Separable Signed Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of list homomorphism complexity for separable signed graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Classification known for separable signed graphs, but not in full generality.

status_evidence.title: List homomorphism problems for signed trees
status_evidence.snippet: Full combinatorial classification accomplished for signed trees with possible loops.
